item.title: At home: Fighting winter's tiny but mighty annoyances
item.description: Winter comes with no shortage of challenges. Between frigid temperatures, blowing snow, and slick ice, no wonder many choose to spend extra time indoors. Alas, winter’s difficulties don’t end at your front door. From aggravating salt stains to poor air quality, here’s how to tackle the season’s most aggravating indoor annoyances. item.title: Hum: Why a Centrepointe butcher shop sells Ottawa's best almond croissants
item.description: At Around the Block Butcher & Market, exceptional house-made baked goods are a surprising find.

item.title: Don't feed the coyotes (or the chipmunks): Coun. Laura Dudas calls for an Ottawa wildlife feeding bylaw
item.description: Ottawa's current animal care and control bylaw addresses domestic animals, but does not specifically regulate the feeding of wildlife

item.title: 'A single bedbug' found at government building in Ottawa after four-day in-office order
item.description: Public Services and Procurement Canada says it took "appropriate measures to quickly address the situation," which included a treatment on the affected area on Feb. 12.

item.title: Team Canada grades: Mitch Marner, Nick Suzuki play heroes in dramatic comeback win over Czechia
item.description: Nick Suzuki saved the day with a late tying goal and Mitch Marner scored the overtime winner, allowing Canadians to finally exhale after an extremely anxious game against Team Czechia.

item.title: Ottawa Senators trying to find 'right fit' for blueline with NHL trade deadline approaching
item.description: There will be only 11 shopping days left until the March 6 NHL trade deadline after the roster freeze is lifted at 11:59 p.m. on Sunday

item.title: Senators Olympic tracker: Tkachuk, Sanderson to play for medal, Stutzle going home
item.description: Brady Tkachuk and Jake Sanderson helped Team USA to a 2-1 overtime victory over Sweden, Nikolas Matinpalo and Finland are moving on, and Tim Stutzle's amazing tournament has come to a close.

item.title: More charges in criminal harassment case, Ottawa police say
item.description: Victims were targeted particularly in shopping centres, on beaches and public transit and in restaurants, police said.
